# Template: numbers.md (machine view)

The numeric-literal inventory: the machine half of number-sync.

**Verdict: script-perfect as an inventory; the sync relation is a
ledger.** Collecting every numeric literal with counts and first
location is mechanical. Whether "3.2" in the abstract and "3.24" in a
table are supposed to be the same number is judgment — that mapping
lives in `dependencies.md` (number-sync invariants), which the skill
cross-checks against this view.

## Format

```markdown
<!-- Machine view. Generated by compile.sh at <stamp> from a scan of
     the prose .tex files (comment lines excluded). REGENERATE: sh
     scripts/compile.sh. -->

# Numbers in prose (numeric literals, by frequency)

| Number | Count | First seen |
|---|---|---|
| 0.9 | 6 | sections/3_method/method.tex:12 ($\theta = 0.9$) |
```

## Source & regeneration

`[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?` over non-comment lines of the prose .tex files;
first-seen keeps file:line and a trimmed context snippet.
`sh scripts/compile.sh numbers`.
